correctness.rationale: Disjoint same-vertex events, exact conditional Bin(n-2,p) parity for distinct vertices, and summation give the finite covariance. Strict monotonicity of q^(n-2)(n-1+nq) proves unique crossing; logarithmic expansion gives critical window and root asymptotics. Twenty-five exact rational graph enumerations and sixteen numerical window checks passed.

originality.rationale: Semantic searches of published mathematical claims for isolated/odd-degree counts, degree-parity correlations, threshold aliases and dense Erdős–Rényi graphs returned no implication-equivalent record; all 99 recoverable same-slot historical claims were screened. Goldstein 2010 and Ghosh–Goldstein–Raič 2011 address marginal or fixed-degree concentration, Alarfaj–Taylor–Bogachev 2023 analyzes numerical-degree correlation, and Janzer–Yip 2025 addresses parity constraints for a different graph property. The new evaluated mixed-count sign boundary and logarithmic profile are not visibly subsumed in inspected material, but further historical equivalence remains a risk.
residual_risks: A general multivariate degree-count generating-function identity may yield the mixed covariance after specialization, although no explicit full sign phase classification was identified.
No exhaustive literature census is claimed; the sign reversal occurs at extremely small absolute covariance.

value.rationale: Isolation and odd-degree counts are canonical local and parity statistics. The theorem isolates an order-parity-dependent dependence reversal, completely classifies finite n and p, and locates a sharp logarithmic dense-graph window. It is not merely a numerical table or an unmotivated slice; the effect size is explicitly qualified.
